title: Newsletters
summary: Sending bulk email to your own lists, and why it goes out in batches.
html:
The newsletter area sends bulk email to lists you build from your own contacts. It is separate from the transactional email that goes with invoices and quotes, which lives in Templates.

Lists and members

A list is a group of recipients. Members can be added from your existing contacts or imported. A contact can be on several lists, and unsubscribing removes them from the one they unsubscribed from.

Writing one

Newsletters use their own templates, so the layout is set once and reused. Write the content, pick the list, and preview it — the preview sends a real message to you, which is the only way to find out what it looks like in the mail client your customers actually use.

Sending, and the queue

A newsletter is not sent in one go. It goes into a queue and is sent in batches by the scheduled task. This is deliberate:

  • Shared hosting enforces an hourly mail limit, and exceeding it gets the rest of the batch dropped silently — or the account suspended.
  • A long send inside a web request would hit the PHP execution time limit partway through.

So if a newsletter shows as sending but recipients are not receiving it, the cron job is the first thing to check. The queue screen shows what has gone and what is waiting.

Bounces

Bounce handling reads a mailbox for delivery failures and marks those addresses, so you stop sending to addresses that do not exist. It is configured under Settings → Newsletter → Bounces and needs the imap extension, the same as tickets.

Statistics

Opens and link clicks are recorded per newsletter. Treat open rates as indicative rather than exact — mail clients that block images do not register an open.

Before your first send

Check your sending address passes SPF and DKIM for your domain. Bulk mail from an address that does not authenticate goes to spam regardless of what this software does. See Configuration for the mail settings.
